back: The aspect the question asks about: benefits, problems, reasons, ways, changes.
Underline the focus, whose/what, and limits (paragraphs, words, time).
A distinct idea that directly answers the summary question; usually one mark each.
Examples, anecdotes, statistics, quotations, repetition, background, off-focus points and opinions.
One sentence can hold two points; one point can be spread over two sentences.
Extract the idea from direct speech: 'I can grow tomatoes all year' → gardens watered year-round.
Write each point briefly, in your own words, and number them to check your total.
Two notes saying the same thing earn only one mark.
Read the whole specified section; points often appear late in a paragraph or in an unexpected paragraph.
